rows.label: Roberto Clemente
rows.hook: got his 3,000th hit in his final regular season and died in a plane crash delivering relief supplies

rows.label: Derek Jeter
rows.description: American former professional baseball player, author, bussinessman and baseball broadcasters
rows.hook: was a longtime shortstop and captain known for the famous backhanded jump throw and his clutch October play

rows.label: Joe DiMaggio
rows.hook: set the record 56-game hitting streak and was known as the Yankee Clipper

rows.label: Lou Gehrig
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Iron Horse for playing 2,130 straight games before a disease that now bears his name

rows.label: Mickey Mantle
rows.hook: was a switch-hitting center fielder famous for tape-measure home runs and a Triple Crown season

rows.label: Don Mattingly
rows.hook: was a beloved first baseman nicknamed Donnie Baseball who won a batting title and MVP but never a World Series

rows.label: Carl Yastrzemski
rows.hook: won a Triple Crown in the Impossible Dream season and later took over left field's famous wall

rows.label: Sandy Koufax
rows.hook: was a dominant lefty ace who threw a perfect game, then retired young because of arthritis

rows.label: Cal Ripken Jr.
rows.hook: broke the record for consecutive games played, earning the nickname the Iron Man

rows.label: Tony Gwynn
rows.description: American Hall of Fame baseball right fielder; 1960-2014
rows.hook: was a lefty hitter nicknamed Mr. Padre who won eight batting titles and hit over .300 in nearly every season

rows.label: Mariano Rivera
rows.description: Panamanian Hall of Fame baseball player, relief pitcher
rows.hook: was the closer with the most saves ever, famous for his cut fastball, and the first unanimous Hall of Famer

rows.label: Clayton Kershaw
rows.hook: is a left-handed ace with a devastating curveball who has won three Cy Young Awards and an MVP

rows.label: Chipper Jones
rows.description: American Hall of Fame baseball player (born 1972)
rows.hook: was a switch-hitting third baseman who spent his entire career with one franchise and won an MVP

rows.label: Yadier Molina
rows.hook: was a defensive-minded catcher famous for controlling the game behind the plate and winning two championships

rows.label: Kirby Puckett
rows.hook: was a stocky center fielder who hit a famous Game 6 walk-off homer to force a Game 7

rows.label: Stan Musial
rows.hook: was a smooth-swinging outfielder nicknamed The Man with 3,630 hits, split evenly between home and road

rows.label: Ernie Banks
rows.hook: was a slugging shortstop nicknamed Mr. Cub who famously said, Let's play two

rows.label: Dustin Pedroia
rows.hook: was a scrappy second baseman nicknamed the Laser Show who won an MVP and two championships

rows.label: George Brett
rows.hook: was a Hall of Fame third baseman with a batting title in three decades and a famous pine tar controversy

rows.label: Buster Posey
rows.description: American baseball executive and former player (born 1987)
rows.hook: was a catcher who won three championships in five years and retired at a young age while still productive

rows.label: Mike Schmidt
rows.description: American professional baseball player, third baseman
rows.hook: was a power-hitting third baseman who won multiple MVPs, hit 548 home runs and was a great fielder

rows.label: Robin Yount
rows.hook: was a shortstop who joined the big leagues as a teenager and later won MVPs at two positions
